draft.title: The expedition to Punt
card: Punt was a land known to the Egyptians for trade, most likely to the south-east of Egypt along the Red Sea. Its exact location is still debated by historians.
In Hatshepsut's reign, a trading expedition sailed to Punt. It is shown in reliefs (carved scenes) on the walls of her temple at Deir el-Bahri.
The ships returned with goods such as myrrh (incense) trees, gold and exotic animals. The reliefs show the trees being carried aboard in baskets.
Hatshepsut had the expedition recorded in her temple. It showed her as a ruler who brought wealth and rare goods to Egypt and who honoured the god Amun.
draft.remember: The Punt reliefs are a main source for a trading expedition that Hatshepsut used to show her success as a ruler.

a.q: What is the main source for the expedition to Punt in Hatshepsut's reign?
opts: Reliefs on the walls of her temple at Deir el-Bahri
Written orders found in the tomb of Thutmose III
Gold objects found at the site of Punt itself
Letters sent by the king of Punt to Egypt
a.why: The expedition is shown in carved reliefs at Deir el-Bahri, and the card names them as the record of it. The tomb of Thutmose III is tempting because he ruled with her, but the card gives no link between his tomb and the expedition.
a.clue: Think about where Hatshepsut chose to record it.

b.q: Why would Hatshepsut want the Punt expedition carved on her temple walls?
opts: It showed her bringing wealth and rare goods to Egypt
It proved that Egypt had never traded with Punt before
It showed that Thutmose III had planned the expedition
It recorded the exact map location of Punt for later rulers
b.why: The reliefs showed a ruler who brought gold, trees and animals to Egypt, which supported her image as a successful pharaoh. The option about a map is tempting, but the card says historians still debate where Punt was, so the reliefs did not settle it.
b.clue: Ask what the goods said about the ruler who gained them.

a.best: Reliefs on the walls of her temple at Deir el-Bahri

b.best: It showed her bringing wealth and rare goods to Egypt
